title: Inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 infection in cellular systems using engineered trimeric receptor-binding domain of spike protein
protocol: Design primers for the RBD region of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein.
Add restriction enzyme cut sites to the 5′ and 3′ ends of the RBD sequence.
Amplify the designed RBD insert using PCR.
Purify the amplified PCR product using a commercial purification kit.
Prepare DNA fragment containing a leader sequence and modified leucine zipper (insert 2).
Add desired restriction enzymes to the 5′ and 3′ ends.
Amplify the region of interest using PCR.
Purify the PCR product using a commercially available PCR purification kit.
Digest the PCR product containing the leader sequence and leucine zipper using HindIII and XhoI.
Digest the PCR product containing the RBD protein using XhoI and XbaI.
Digest a mammalian expression vector (e.g., pcDNA3) using HindIII and XbaI.
Purify the vector and inserts by running DNA on an agarose gel and excising the appropriate bands.
Prepare the final volume of the vector and inserts to 30 μL.
Ligate the inserts into the vector with T4 DNA ligase.
Incubate the reaction at 21°C–25°C for 30 min.
Thaw competent bacteria.
Aliquot of competent bacteria.
Mix 2 μL of the ligation mix with 25 μL of competent cells.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 10 min.
Incubate the mixture on a heating block at 42°C for 30 s.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 10 min.
Spread the mixture onto a prewarmed 10 cm agar culture plate containing LB medium and ampicillin (100 μg/mL).
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 16 h.
Select individual colonies and inoculate them in a miniculture of 2 mL liquid LB with ampicillin at 100 μg/mL.
Incubate the minicultures at 37°C for 8–12 hours on a shaking incubator set to 220 rpm.
Isolate plasmid DNA using a commercially available miniprep kit.
Digest isolated plasmids with HindIII and XbaI enzymes.
Run digestion products on an agarose gel.
Verify the presence of RBD protein in the vector by sequencing using the primer: 5′- CGCAAATGGGCGGTAGGCGTG.
Purify verified DNA construct.
Transfer 250 μL of miniculture into a maxiculture of 200 mL autoclaved LB medium supplemented with ampicillin at 100 μg/mL.
Incubate the maxicultures at 37°C for 12–16 hours on a shaking incubator set to 220 rpm.
Isolate plasmid DNA using a commercially available maxiprep kit.
Incubate DNA at 21°C–25°C for 10–15 min after preparing the Ca3(PO4)2 mixture.
Add DNA/Ca3(PO4)2 mixture to cells drop wise.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 6 h after adding the DNA mixture.
Wash plates 2 times with 10 mL sterile PBS each time, performing washes very gently.
Add 20 mL of fresh, prewarmed growth media for HEK293T cells.
Incubate plates at 37°C for 72 h.
Collect cell supernatant in conical tubes after incubation.
Centrifuge to remove cell debris from collected supernatant.
Pass cell supernatant through a 0.45 μm syringe filter.
Clip a gravity column onto a stand.
Close the column flow.
Slowly add 10 mL of Ni-NTA beads into gravity flow column using a serological pipette.
Allow beads to settle to the bottom of the column for 10 min.
Open the column flow to allow ethanol to drain.
Change column flow rate to 1 mL/min.
Slowly add 100 mL of Equilibration Buffer through the column.
Pass RBD conditioned media through the column with equilibrated NiNTA beads.
Collect flow-through media in a clean 1 L glass bottle.
Change column flow rate to 2 mL/min.
Pass the flow-through through column to increase the amount of RBD bound to NiNTA beads.
Flow 20 mL of Equilibration Buffer through the column.
Flow 20 mL of Wash Buffer A through the column.
Flow 20 mL of Wash Buffer B through the column.
Flow 20 mL of Wash Buffer C through the column.
Change column flow rate to 1 mL/min.
Elute bound RBD with 20 mL of Elution Buffer into a clean 50 mL conical tube.
Transfer 20 mL of eluted RBD fraction to dialysis tube.
Secure both ends of the dialysis tube with a clamp.
Place the bag in a 5 L glass beaker.
Fill the beaker with 4 L of Tris-NaCl buffer.
Use a magnetic stirrer on the lowest setting.
Allow dialysis to occur for 12 hours at 4°C.
Add sample to the top compartment of a Millipore concentration tube with a molecular weight cutoff of 50 kDa.
Centrifuge at 4000 g for 5 minutes at 4°C and discard the flow through.
Repeat this process in the same Millipore concentrator tube until all of the dialyzed RBD has been concentrated.
Centrifuge concentrated RBD fraction at 10,000 g in a tabletop mini centrifuge for 10 minutes at 4°C to remove any precipitates that may clog the column.
Equilibrate Mono Q column in an AKTA FPLC system with Tris-NaCl buffer A.
Inject samples into a Mono Q column and collect the flow through.
Add more Tris-NaCl buffer A in batches depending on the capacity of the column and collect 15 more fractions.
Generate tRBD as a secreted protein from HEK-293T cells into the growth media.
Purify tRBD using a Mono Q anion exchange column to remove major contaminants like BSA and other proteins.
Collect early flowthrough fractions 3–8 in equilibration buffer A for tRBD purification.
Elute bound proteins with a salt gradient using Tris-NaCl buffer B containing 1 M NaCl.
Carefully adjust the flow rate of buffer A and buffer B to obtain a salt gradient over time.
Elute proteins binding to the column with varying affinity.
Determine the number of fractions to be collected based on protein content in the eluate.
Take 30 μL from each fraction.
Dilute the samples with 10 μL 4× Laemmli buffer.
Boil the diluted samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Vortex and quickly spin down samples in a tabletop centrifuge for 5 min at 10,000 g.
Clip the previously prepared 10% polyacrylamide gel into a gel runner tank.
Pour 1× Running Buffer into the gel running tank chamber to cover the top of the gel.
Load the samples from step 27 into the gel.
Place the safety lid with electrodes over the entire apparatus.
Plug the electrodes into a power pack and run the gel for 100V for 10 min, then 200V for 55 min at 21°C–25°C.
Submerge an open Transfer Cassette plate into a tray with 1× transfer buffer.
Place the sponge support pad on top of the cathode plate in the cassette.
Add filter paper to the cassette.
Attach the acrylamide gel to the cassette.
Place the nitrocellulose membrane on top of the gel.
Add another layer of filter paper.
Place a sponge support pad on top.
Submerge and saturate each layer with premade 1× transfer buffer prior to use.
Gently use a roller to remove any air bubbles after adding each layer.
Gently close the transfer plate with the anode plate and place the assembled cassette into the transfer tank.
Adjust the buffer level until 1× transfer buffer submerges the necessary level within the tank.
Move the power pack and transfer tank to 4°C or place it in an ice tray to prevent overheating.
Connect the electrodes into the power pack.
Run for 1 h at a constant voltage of 100 V.
Dialyze and concentrate protein elution as described.
Pause point: Aliquot purified tRBD.
Store aliquoted tRBD at -80°C until use.
Dilute 30 μL of tRBD conditioned media or purified tRBD with 4× Laemmli Sample buffer.
Boil diluted samples at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Vortex and quickly spin down boiled samples in a tabletop mini-centrifuge for at least 5 seconds.
Resolve samples on SDS-PAGE and transfer to nitrocellulose membrane.
Analyze western blot bands using the Gel Analyzer tool of ImageJ (NIH).
Prepare standard curve using densitometry values of known concentrations of commercially available recombinant RBD.
Adjust concentration of 50 μL of purified tRBD to 20 μg/mL with PBS.
Preheat the 2.5% glutaraldehyde solution at 80°C.
Add 3 μL of 2.5% glutaraldehyde to 20 μL of 20 μg/mL purified tRBD.
Incubate at 80°C for 5 minutes.
Stop the crosslinking reaction by adding 3 μL of 1 M Tris-HCl.
Add 9 μL of 4× Laemmli Sample buffer without beta mercaptoethanol (BME).
Heat sample at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Prepare a control sample of purified tRBD and add 9 μL of 4× Laemmli Sample buffer with BME as a reducing agent.
Resolve samples on 10% SDS-PAGE gel.
Transfer the resolved samples onto nitrocellulose membrane.
Probe with antibody detecting HIS or FLAG tag or RBD itself.
Plate 1.25 × 10^4 HEK293T-ACE2 cells/well in a flat bottom 96 well plate.
Incubate cells for 16–24 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Pre-coat culture dish with polylysine to facilitate cell adherence if necessary.
Incubate cells with 100 μL of SARS-CoV-2 or VSV-G pseudovirus and/or 50 ng of tRBD.
Add 5 μg/mL polybrene to each well to facilitate lentiviral infection.
Adjust final volume of each well to 200 μL.
Incubate for 48 hours at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Gently wash cells with 100 μL of PBS to remove cell media.
Directly lyse cells on plate by adding 20 μL of 1× Passive Lysis Buffer from the manufacturer’s kit.
Allow samples to shake in lysis buffer at room temperature (21°C–25°C) for 15 min.
Prepare plate reader to read luminescence with a 2 s delay and 10 s read time.
Centrifuge the lysate for 10,000 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer 10 μL of the cell lysate supernatant/well of a white clear bottom 96 well plate.
Dispense 50 μL of pre-thawed LARII solution and quickly pipette up and down 4–5 times to obtain a homogenous mix of lysate and LARII.
Place plate in microplate reader with luminescence reading capacity.
Plot the graph using relative luminescence unit (RLU) readings obtained as described.
Keep LARII reagent in dark until ready to use.
Read luminescence immediately, as signal will decrease with time.
Plate 1 × 10^5 Vero E6 cells per well in a 24-well plate 24 hours prior to infection.
Prepare tRBD and mock conditioned media to the desired concentration in virus medium.
Incubate cells with 250 μl of tRBD or mock dilution for 30 minutes at 37°C, gently rocking after 15 minutes.
Infect each well with 50 μl of previously prepared SARS-CoV-2 true virus at a dilution of 10^-4.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 1 hour.
Gently rock the plate every 15 minutes during incubation.
Overlay each well with 500 μl of media containing DMEM, 0.05% agarose, and 2% FBS.
Incubate the plate at 37°C for 72 hours post-infection.
Fix cells with 4% formaldehyde solution diluted in PBS for 30 minutes.
Stain with crystal violet for 5 minutes.
Calculate viral titers of SARS-CoV-2 true virus.
Count plaque forming units per well for each dilution.
Normalize each dilution to well with Mock media.
